column1: # Manual smoke-onset annotations for the FIRESENSE positive videos.
# The onset of a positive video is the first frame at which smoke is
# *unambiguously visible* to a human annotator. The values were obtained by
# inspecting 4x4 contact sheets of the whole video and a finer 4x4 contact
# sheet of the first 120 frames (tools/make_contact_sheet.py); the sheets are
# In 12 of the 13 positive videos the smoke is already visible in the first
# frame: the clips were cut starting from the moment the smoke was produced.
# The videos therefore contain almost no "pre-onset" frames. The consequence
# for the benchmark is spelled out in paper/dataset_card.md and
# paper/benchmark_protocol.md: the classical "detection delay from the
# annotated onset" degenerates into the "time to first alarm"
# onset coincides with the start of the clip.
# `official_onset_frame` records the first frame that carries the cyan
# smoke-region contour burned into the recording (only a subset of the videos
# were produced with the annotation overlay). It is reported as a cross-check
# and is deliberately NOT used for the primary metric
